subject: Launch-day surge contingency, SKU repricing and short-window credit
messages:
From: Leah Morales <leah.morales@brightstore.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@brightstore.com
Date: 2026-12-28T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Short-window throttle bump + pricing for Dec 31 launch

Kimberly —

Thanks again for the call earlier. We’re planning a feature launch on Dec 31 that will drive a concentrated 36–48 hour spike of inference traffic. Our engineering team estimates a short-term 4–6x uplift in QPS for the first 24 hours.

Two asks: 1) Can you temporarily elevate our rate limit/quota for the 12/31–1/1 window to avoid early throttling? 2) We need clarity on how overrun will be billed (per-token overage vs one-off burst SKU) and whether BrightStore can get a short-term grace credit for launch instability.

We can provide a forecast (attached) and we’re prepared to sign a PO amendment if needed.

Leah
Leah Morales
Head of Platform, BrightStore
leah.morales@brightstore.com

Attachment: brightstore-launch-traffic-forecast.xlsx (xlsx)

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Leah Morales <leah.morales@brightstore.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, procurement@brightstore.com
Date: 2026-12-28T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short-window throttle bump + pricing for Dec 31 launch

Leah —

Thanks for the forecast — that helps. Short answers up front: yes, we can provision a temporary headroom uplift and we can put a capped, one-time credit on the table for launch-related instability. I outlined two practical options below so your procurement team can decide quickly.

Option A — Temporary "burst SKU":
- 48-hour window starting when you flip to prod (you tell us start time)
- Flat burst SKU: $5,500 flat fee for up to 60M extra tokens during the window; after that standard overrun rates apply
- No change to monthly commit; we invoice the flat fee and apply a one-time $1,500 launch credit if production errors cause throttled requests

Option B — Elevated quota + blended overrun pricing:
- 48-hour quota increase to X requests/min (we’ll confirm exact number after ingesting forecast)
- Overrun billed at a blended per-token rate of $0.015/token (vs your standard $0.018), capped at $6,000 for the window
- If you commit to a 6-month minimum headroom profile post-launch, we can apply a 10% discount to the blended overrun for that period

Next steps I suggest: pick A or B, confirm a start time, and procurement sends a PO referencing the attached amendment draft. If you need legal redlines we can fast-track. Ben — I’m CCing you for approval on the one-time credit/concession if BrightStore wants Option A.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

Attachment: draft-amendment-template (pdf)

From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Leah Morales <leah.morales@brightstore.com>, procurement@brightstore.com
Date: 2026-12-29T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short-window throttle bump + pricing for Dec 31 launch

Kim / Monica —

I reviewed both options. Give BrightStore the following concession so they don’t have to rebuild a last-minute mitigation:
- Approve Option A with a reduction: burst SKU fee lowered to $4,200 (from $5,500)
- One-time instability credit increased to $2,500 (applied as invoice credit if we confirm throttling-related failed calls)
- Legal to sign the attached one-page amendment (no changes to core T&C)

Reasoning: BrightStore has been a steady customer; a small concession now preserves the renewal trajectory. Approve me to proceed and I’ll issue guidance to finance for quick invoicing.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

----
On Dec 29, 2026, at 07:58, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com wrote:
> Ben — I’ll confirm finance flow. If procurement needs a faster e-sign path, we can use DocuSign link and attach the reduced fee in the payment terms.

Attachment: none

From: Leah Morales <leah.morales@brightstore.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@brightstore.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-12-29T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short-window throttle bump + pricing for Dec 31 launch

Thanks Kim and Ben — that works for us. We’ll take Option A with Ben’s concession. Procurement will route a PO for $4,200 and we’ll request DocuSign for the amendment. Can we confirm the exact quota bump (requests/min) you’ll provision? We want to ensure our rollout plan aligns.

Leah

P.S. We appreciate the quick turnaround — appreciate the extra credit if anything goes sideways.

Attachment: procurement-intent.pdf (pdf)

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Leah Morales <leah.morales@brightstore.com>, procurement@brightstore.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-12-30T17:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short-window throttle bump + pricing for Dec 31 launch

Leah / Procurement —

Confirming next actions and operational details:
- Quota bump: We’ll provision +5x QPS relative to your current peak, which our infra team maps to ~5,000 additional concurrent requests (we’ll provide the exact requests/min by 11:00 PT tomorrow)
- Start window: Please confirm your production flip ETA (we’re standing by to start the 48-hour window when you go live)
- DocuSign: I’ve uploaded the one-page amendment with the approved burst fee of $4,200 and $2,500 instability credit. Link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/XYZ-AMPLIFY-20261230
- Invoice: Finance will issue an invoice for $4,200 upon signature; the instability credit is applied as a post-event invoice adjustment if validated by logs

I’m also attaching a clean PDF of the amendment for procurement to review before e-signing.

Good luck on launch tomorrow — ping me if you want ops on the war-room.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: 12-30-amendment-draft.pdf (pdf)
